title: Sustained vs Spike: cost & latency timeline (bench draft)
body:
PURPOSE:
Quick experimental draft comparing two realistic workload shapes (sustained medium QPS vs short high-amplitude spike) to show tradeoffs in tail latency, token-level cost, and effective SLO exposure. This is a working note for the observability + serving runtime sync on 11/25 — rough numbers, heuristics, and open questions at the bottom.

SUMMARY (tl;dr):
- Sustained workload (steady 100 QPS, 30–60m): good batching, p50/p90/p99 = 40/120/280 ms, cost per 1M tokens = $45.
- Spike workload (3x–20x for 20–90s): batching drops, cold slots + scheduling contention -> p50/p90/p99 = 65/420/1900 ms, cost per 1M tokens = $160 (higher due to unamortized slot time and extra headroom).
- For SLOs that care about p99 under bursts, the effective cost to hit the same p99 is ~3–4x higher than the steady-state cost.

EXPERIMENT SETUP (short):
- Model: 7B quantized variant (production-like kernels), sequence length mean 128 tokens, generation avg 60 tokens.
- Hardware: A2-class GPU pool (mix of older+newer nodes, representative of Dedicated).
- Routing policy: prefer local-region, fallback to warm spare nodes when overloaded.
- Two workload shapes: sustained_100 (100 sustained qps for 45m), spike_3k_short (baseline 100 qps, ramp to 3000 qps over 6s, hold 30s, decay 10s).
- Measurement: client-observed latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), tokens served, GPU-time, number of active slots, queuing time. Cost is modeled as amortized infra cost + extra slot overhead during spike.

TEXT CHART: timeline of qps and p99 (annotated)
(legend: - = low, = = med, # = high)
QPS:  |--------------------------SUSTAINED_100---------------------------| 45m
       --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       0        10m       20m       30m       40m       45m

SPIKE (30s window):  baseline---===#######===---baseline
                    0s   6s  12s  18s  24s  30s  40s

p99 latency (approx relative):
SUSTAINED_100:  280ms steady (small jitter +-40ms)
SPIKE window:   250ms -> 1.9s peak -> decays to 320ms over 60s

SIMPLE TABLE (human-readable):
Scenario | avg QPS | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens served | est cost per 1M tokens
-------- | ------- | -------- | -------- | -------- | ------------- | ---------------------
Sustained_100 | 100 | 40 | 120 | 280 | 2.7M (45m) | $45
Spike_3k_short | 100 -> 3k spike | 65 | 420 | 1900 | 3.1M (45m window incl spike) | $160

NOTES ON COST MODEL (informal):
- Baseline infra cost amortized across steady throughput gives the $45/1M tokens. Assumes batching/kvcache hit rates ~60% and slot utilization 70%.
- Spike cost inflated due to: (1) more short-lived slots spun up that aren't fully utilized; (2) lower batching (only smaller batches fit in tight latency windows); (3) fallback to higher-cost variants for priority requests.
- We did not include optional pre-warm or predictive warm policies — those reduce tail but raise baseline cost.

OBSERVATIONS (what surprised us):
- p90 increases earlier in the ramp than p99 (predictable) but p99 jumps nonlinearly when scheduler hits queue pressure (we saw a cliff around 1.2k qps).
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~18% during the spike window because more unique prefixes hit the system, which amplified token work.
- Short (20–40s) spikes are the worst from a cost-per-token perspective because autoscaling granularity + billing windows cause significant wasted headroom.

QUANTITATIVE SENSITIVITY (rough heuristics):
- If batching efficiency drops by 30% during spike, cost per 1M tokens increases ~2.8x.
- If we pre-warm a small pool to absorb the first 1k qps of spike (idle cost ~20% of active), p99 is cut by ~40% during spike but baseline cost increases by ~8%.

RECOMMENDATIONS (short bullets):
- For workload owners with frequent short spikes, consider hybrid strategy: keep a small warm pool + priority routing for critical paths.
- Add a "burst tax" visualization in Console showing estimated cost delta for recent spikes (per-route). Make it visible in the cost timeline.
- Run a follow-up experiment with predictive pre-warm (based on request-rate derivative) vs fixed warm pool and measure net cost to meet p99 target.

OPEN QUESTIONS / ACTION ITEMS:
- Q1: How does different model size quantization interact? (7B vs 13B vs 70B) -> booking slot shapes differ. (owner: Rajiv)
- Q2: Should Dedicated contracts include explicit burst SLAs or guidance? What pricing add-on covers predictable reserve for bursts? (owner: Lina)
- Q3: Is our autoscaler reacting fast enough or are scheduling bottlenecks in the job launcher? Need traces (owner: Marcus)

EXTRA: SHORT CHECKLIST FOR NEXT RUN
- [ ] Re-run with deterministic KV-cache pattern (same prefixes) to isolate batching effect
- [ ] Run with pre-warm 10% pool and capture cost/time series per route
- [ ] Add per-token energy estimate for transparency (opt in)

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING THOUGHTS:
- We should build a short Console widget that overlays qps + p99 + estimated extra cost for the last 24h, with a slider to simulate pre-warm size. Most PMs/SREs will grok that quickly.
- This doc will be pared down to a one-pager for the 11/25 sync; keep the heuristics table and the open questions.

REFERENCES/IDS: see linked artifacts above for the spike handling Linear ticket and runtime PR.

END.
